rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī introduces the prohibition of prayer as one manifestation of human tyranny and as the occasion for a warning.
rows.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl vowed to trample the Prophet while he prayed; when he approached he recoiled, describing fire, terror, and wings, and the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb; the sūra’s end was revealed. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the preventer as Umayya b. Khalaf, who forbade Salmān to pray; al-Ālūsī says this is hardly sound because Salmān accepted Islam in Medina after the Hijra while the sūra is Meccan, though the verse’s general warning would include Umayya if the incident occurred.
rows.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the prayer was ẓuhr; another account says it was Islam’s first congregational prayer, with the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī, and that Abū Ṭālib urged Jaʿfar to join his cousin and left happily, composing verses in their support.
rows.anchor: على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer was obligatory on the Miʿrāj, usually dated one year before Hijra (Ibn Ḥazm says consensus; Ibn Fāris says 1y3m, al-Suddī 1y5m); Abū Ṭālib died about three years before Hijra, before Khadīja by three or five days, while she died ten years after the mission.
rows.anchor: الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī’s reported dating places the Miʿrāj five years after the beginning of the mission; Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits it, and al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī prefer it, though al-Ālūsī notes objections to that chronology.
rows.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين لكن قيل عليه ما قيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take yanha as ‘prevents’; al-Ālūsī says this wording suggests Abū Jahl could only attempt to prevent the prayer, not do more.
rows.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl verbally challenged the Prophet while he prayed, asking whether he had not forbidden him; al-Tirmidhī authenticates this report.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb evokes the past scene as if it were happening now, lending vividness to its strange character.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On one analysis, raʾayta is cognitive, as in 96:13: the first object is the relative clause’s referent, while later objects are elided or resumed by a pronoun or demonstrative; the third question’s second object is ‘Does he not know that God sees?’
rows.anchor: الرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example with repeated akhbirnī is not syntactic tanāzuʿ: clauses cannot be elided as such, and the construction instead involves semantic demand and deletion outside tanāzuʿ.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clauses’ apodoses are omitted because ‘Does he not know?’ indicates them; another analysis lets raʾayta itself anticipate the subsequently stated matter.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه ويقدر حسبما تقتضيه الصناعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concealed subjects of kāna and the verbs following it refer to the person forbidding prayer.
rows.anchor: والضمائر المستترة في { كان } وما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾayta means ‘tell me’: because seeing leads to knowing, asking whether one has seen stands for asking about what was seen.
rows.anchor: والمراد من أرأيت أخبرني فإن الرؤية لما كانت سبباً للعلم أجري الاستفهام عنها مجرى الاستخبار عن متعلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This use of raʾayta as inquiry is said to work with either visual or cognitive seeing; grammarians have two positions on the construction.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإجراء على ما يفهم من كلام بعض الأئمة يكون مع الرؤية البصرية والرؤية القلبية وللنحاة فيه قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the tanwīn on ʿabdan as indefiniteness and the time phrase as indicating that the prohibition occurs while the person is praying.
rows.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses are separated so each denunciation and threat stands on its own, heightening the censure and warning.
rows.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads a three-stage escalation: the first threat censures the prohibition without specifying the preventer’s state, the next addresses his claimed righteousness, and the last his actual denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority do not restrict the two conditional descriptions as al-Ālūsī’s staged analysis does: they contrast claimed right guidance or piety with the preventer’s actual denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes both conditions lead to the same point: the first feigns latitude before mocking the notion that forbidding worship and urging idols could be guidance; the second mockingly grants a condition everyone knows is false.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن الشرط الثاني تكرار للأول لأن معنى الأول أنه ليس على الهدى وأوضح بأن إدخال حرف الشرط في الأول لإرخاء العنان صورة والتهكم حقيقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse makes raʾayta in the first question visual and in the second and third cognitive; the final question’s answer is explicit, while the prior conditional points forward to it.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parse, leaving the last question uncoordinated marks it as independently actual and makes its answer an ensuing threat; the earlier conditions merely widen the scope.
rows.anchor: ولم تعطف الأخيرة على ما قبلها للإيذان باستقلالها بالوقوع في نفس الأمر وباستتباع الوعيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further analysis treats all three questions as cognitive and the second as a repetition of the first; both conditions fill its second-object slot, with the final answer explicit and the first answer elided.
rows.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني للأولى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī permits an interrogative conditional apodosis without faʾ and cites 6:47; al-Raḍī accepts this, but Abū Ḥayyān and al-Damāmīnī object that an interrogative requires faʾ, absent here.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري في كشافه وارتضاه الرضي واستشهد له

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says he knows no one who allows an interrogative sentence to answer a condition without faʾ; al-Damāmīnī likewise finds it problematic to parse ‘Will anyone perish?’ as the apodosis without the required faʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and others object that raʾayta’s second object must be an interrogative or oath clause, not a conditional; al-Khafājī answers that the conditional and its interrogative answer can occupy that slot, as al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī allow, consistent with Sibawayh’s preferred view.
rows.anchor: واعترض أيضاً جعل الجملة الشرطية في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee is left outside both the preventer and the worshipper because the context calls for an observer distinct from them.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي عن مورد الخطاب

rows.speaker: جمع
rows.claim: A group takes the address throughout as directed to anyone capable of understanding; another view makes it address ‘the human,’ as in 96:8.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr prefers the Prophet as the addressee; another view allows the unbelieving preventer, while other proposals assign the questions to the Prophet or to anyone fit to understand.
rows.anchor: جعله للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجوز غيره جعله للكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the tanwīn on ‘a servant’ to magnify the Prophet, heighten the enormity of the prohibition, and intensify the wonder it provokes.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في عبداً لتفخيمه عليه الصلاة والسلام واستعظام النهي وتأكيد التعجيب منه

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam reads the second question as asking whether guidance and commanding piety would not better suit this rational, wealthy man than disbelief and opposition to God; it laments his loss of high rank for a base one.
rows.anchor: أرأيت إن صار على الهدى واشتغل بأمر نفسه أما كان يليق به ذلك إذ هو رجل عاقل ذو ثروة

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn sees the first question as exposing the tyranny of a self-satisfied person who goes beyond ingratitude to urge disbelief; the next questions rebuke lost guidance and piety, then earned punishment and distance from God.
rows.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī presents the preceding readings for reflection and leaves God’s intended meaning ultimately known to Him.
rows.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second question mentions commanding piety because forbidding something commands its opposite or entails that command; its mention there may supply what was omitted from the first question.
rows.anchor: لأن النهي عن الشيء أمر بضده أو مستلزم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the first question omits the command to piety, included in the second, because prayer is practical worship and a stronger example of calling others than verbal instruction.
rows.anchor: واقتصر على ذكر الصلاة ولم يعكس لأن الأمر بالتقوى دعوة قولية والصلاة دعوة فعلية والفعل أقوى من القول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the first phrase describes forbidding someone while he is praying, not necessarily forbidding prayer itself; the prohibition could concern prayer or another matter.
rows.anchor: وقيل المذكور أولاً ليس النهي عن الصلاة بل النهي حين الصلاة وهو محتمل أن يكون لها أو لغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the threat applies to anyone who prevents prayer; it does not forbid objections to prayer in usurped property or disliked times, since the objection targets an accompanying quality rather than prayer itself.
rows.anchor: الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report says ʿAlī saw people praying before the Eid prayer and said he had not seen the Prophet do that; asked why he did not stop them, he feared the verse’s threat. Another version says he preferred to relate the Prophet’s practice rather than forbid a worshipper.
rows.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa similarly avoids direct prohibition: when Abū Yūsuf asks what a worshipper should say after rising from bowing, he gives the preferred phrase and instruction to prostrate without explicitly forbidding the alternative.
rows.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caution about forbidding prayer extends to forbidding other forms of worship; verbal commands and circumstantial interference alike count, including distracting someone from worship, a common failing.
rows.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي
